content_of_post_to_comment: Very few teachers leave teaching just because it’s a difficult job. They leave because they don’t feel trusted, they’re not supported, and (this is the big one) they feel their work is meaningless.
comment: The meaning problem is interesting because it suggests retention isn't just about workload. A teacher can endure difficulty when they see impact, but even a manageable job becomes draining when the feedback loop between effort and purpose breaks.
